title: The Definite Article and Adjectives
description: The article marks a noun as definite. This unit connects article use with adjective agreement and introduces attributive and predicative functions.

blocks.html: The definite article is a prefix, commonly הַ, attached to the noun. In many forms it is followed by a doubled consonant; gutturals and resh resist doubling, so the article's vowel may change. An attributive adjective agrees with its noun in gender and number and generally takes the article when the noun is definite. A predicate adjective makes a statement about a subject and often remains indefinite. Use both word order and definiteness to tell the constructions apart.

didYouKnow: According to OSHB/MorphHB (CC BY 4.0), the most frequent word in this unit is הַמֶּלֶךְ (hammeleḵ), occurring 1 times in the Westminster Leningrad Codex.
